questions.prompt: Match each SOLID letter to its principle.
questions.explanation: SOLID stands for Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, and Dependency Inversion.

questions.prompt: The Open/Closed Principle says software entities should be:

options.text: Open for extension but closed for modification
Open source but closed to outside contributors
Closed for extension but open for modification

questions.explanation: OCP means you add new behavior by adding new code, without editing existing, already-tested code.

questions.prompt: A Penguin class extends Bird but overrides fly() to throw an error. Which principle does this most clearly violate?
questions.explanation: A Penguin can't stand in for a Bird wherever fly() is called, so it breaks substitutability — an LSP violation the compiler won't catch.

questions.prompt: The 'D' in SOLID is the Dependency ____ Principle: depend on abstractions, not concretions.
questions.explanation: Dependency Inversion: high-level code and low-level details both depend on an abstraction in the middle.

questions.prompt: Which statements about Dependency Inversion (DIP), Dependency Injection (DI), and Inversion of Control (IoC) are TRUE? Select all that apply.

options.text: DIP is a principle: depend on abstractions
DI is a technique: pass dependencies in instead of creating them internally
DI, DIP, and IoC are three names for exactly the same thing
DI is a Gang of Four design pattern

questions.explanation: DIP is the principle, DI is a technique that achieves it, and IoC is the broader idea — they are related but distinct. DI is not one of the 23 GoF patterns.

questions.prompt: Splitting a fat AllInOne { print, scan, fax } interface into separate Printer and Scanner interfaces follows which principle?
questions.explanation: ISP says prefer small, client-specific interfaces so a class isn't forced to implement methods (like fax) it doesn't use.
